transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m just tired all the time. Not just normal after-school tired. Even if I sleep through the night, I still feel like I have to force myself through grading, making dinner, getting ready for the next day.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like?

Some things, I guess. I can still smile at school and get through lessons, but… when I get home it’s like everything feels kind of gray. Even things I used to like, like my garden or painting with watercolors, feel far away.
Do you still find pleasure in the things you used to enjoy, or has that changed?

It’s changed, I think. I can still… you know, smile at school and do what I need to do for the kids. But most days underneath it feels kind of flat. Like there’s this gray feeling that comes home with me, and things like my garden or watercolors just feel… far away.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?
Not really the way I used to. I can still put on a smile for my students and get through the day, but when I’m home… everything feels kind of flat. Even my garden or painting, they just feel distant.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes… I think so. I still manage to seem okay at school, smile for the students and get through lessons, but underneath it’s just kind of gray. When I get home, even things like my garden or watercolors feel… distant.
Have you been having any thoughts about hurting yourself or wishing you weren't alive?
I… don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt low, but not like I want to hurt myself.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About… a little over two years. Maybe two years and a couple months. It started around when my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine changed.
Have you experienced a decrease in energy levels?

Yes. I’m tired pretty much all the time. Not just… normal teacher tired. Even if I sleep through the night, I still have to really push myself to get through grading, dinner, and getting ready for the next morning.
Have you experienced a loss of interest in social activities?

Yeah… I guess I have. I still do what I need to do for my students and at home, but I don’t really go out much anymore. I’ve pulled back from things like mentoring and… the creative stuff I used to make time for. It just doesn’t feel as full as it used to.
Have you experienced significant changes in your appetite or weight?
Um… not really significant, I don’t think. My appetite might go up and down a little, but I haven’t noticed any major weight change.
Have you experienced a marked reduction in productivity?

Some, yeah. I’m still showing up for my students and for my family, but… I’ve definitely pulled back from extra things. Mentoring, going out, my creative routines. I don’t really keep up with those like I used to.
Do you feel like your low mood is interfering with your ability to function at work or at home?

A little, yeah. I’m still getting to work and taking care of things at home, but I’ve pulled back from… extra things, I guess. Mentoring, going out, the creative routines I used to have. It’s not like everything’s fallen apart, but it does feel smaller.
Do you feel like your low mood is consistently present throughout the day?

Most days, yeah… it’s kind of there in the background. I can still smile for my students and get through lessons, but underneath it feels gray and flat. Then I go home and even things I usually like, like the garden or watercolors, feel… far away.
Would you say your low mood is mild, or is it interfering significantly with your daily life?

I’d say it’s mild. I’m still showing up for my students and my family. I just… don’t do as much beyond that anymore. Mentoring, social plans, the creative stuff I used to keep up with—it’s kind of fallen away.
Is your low mood present every day?

Most days, yes. I can usually get through work and smile for my students, but underneath there’s this gray, flat feeling… and it tends to follow me home. Even my garden or watercolors feel kind of far away.
Would you describe your current low mood as mildly interfering with your daily life or significantly interfering with it?
Mildly, I think. I’m still getting to work and being there for my family… but I’ve pulled back from things like mentoring, seeing people, and the creative routines I used to have.
Would you say that your low mood is affecting your relationships with family and friends?

A little, yes. I’m still there for my family, and I keep up with work, but I’ve sort of… stopped saying yes to social things. And I don’t really do the mentoring or creative routines I used to. I guess I’m more withdrawn than I’d like to admit.
Would you say your low mood is making it hard to do everyday tasks like taking care of yourself or managing your household?

Not really the basic stuff, no. I’m still showing up for my students and my family. It’s more that I’ve let go of… extra things, I guess. Mentoring, going out socially, my creative routines. Those are the things that have kind of slipped.
Has your low mood lasted for two weeks or more?

Yes… definitely more than two weeks. It’s been, um, about two years now—maybe two years and a couple months. It started around when my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine changed.
Would you say your low mood is significantly interfering with your daily life now?

Somewhat, yes. I’m still getting to work and taking care of my family, but I’ve pulled back from a lot of the other things… mentoring, going out, the creative routines I used to have. It makes life feel a lot smaller.
